artifacts.caption: FIG. 1 is a graph depicting an example of a TMA chart of a polyethylene porous base material and a separator. For example, as depicted in FIG. 1 , the following shrinkage peaks A and B may be present. That is, in the case of the composite separator having a polyethylene porous membrane (PE membrane) and a heat-resistant porous layer including aramid or the like, a lamellar crystal occurs in the PE membrane at some point exceeding 100° C. to cause shrinkage, and a first shrinkage peak A appears near 135° C. After that, due to increased temperature, the shrink is temporarily recovered. When the temperature further increases, a so-called extended-chain crystal occurs in which the molecules have been aligned in a lengthwise direction thereof and a second shrinkage peak B appears near 150° C. In this case, in the composite separator, a single shrinkage peak C appears near 150° C. In a high temperature region of from around 150° C. to around 250° C., extension per 1° C. increase is a slow extension of less than 0.5%.
